title: AEZ KDF Security Properties and Interface
summary: AEZ currently derives subkeys from arbitrary-length keys via Extract, but the KDF's required security properties and proper interface remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For AEZ, an arbitrary-length byte-string key $K \in \mathrm{Byte}^{*}$ is processed by a key-derivation function named Extract to produce three 16-byte subkeys $(I,J,L)$, with the current interface $\text{Extract}: \mathrm{Byte}^{*} \to \mathrm{Byte}^{48}$; the definition of Extract is omitted from the AEZ figures and treated as orthogonal to the rest of AEZ. It remains unresolved which security properties a suitable KDF for this arbitrary-length key processing should provide and what interface or signature that KDF should have.

scope.domain: Key-derivation design for the AEZ authenticated-encryption construction.
parameters: Extract: key-derivation function producing the subkeys
I, J, and L: three 16-byte derived subkeys
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the security properties a suitable KDF should provide and its appropriate interface or signature.

citations.label: Robust Authenticated-Encryption AEZ and the Problem That It Solves

progress.summary: The paper omits Extract's definition from the AEZ figures as orthogonal to the rest of the construction and records its current arbitrary-length-input, 48-byte-output interface. It explicitly states that a good KDF's security properties and even its signature are unresolved.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., Robust Authenticated-Encryption AEZ and the Problem That It Solves
